感觉 AI 做游戏已经是 Vibe Coding 之后另一个非常稳定且很有前景的用例了。

针对网页游戏做了大量优化，内置很多工具帮你让游戏在网页里顺畅跑起来。

最顶的是在发布上做了很多工作，支持一键发布到 Google Play。以往对很多开发者来说挺难搞的变现环节，现在做出来的小游戏能直接拿来赚钱。

text:
Sean Goedecke 在个人博客发文说，在大型软件项目里，程序员只理解自己负责的那一部分代码是正常的，而且这已经是能做到的最好状态。

确实如此，我基于原文稍微解读和引申一下。

很多人说 AI 写不好程序，因为 AI 不能完整理解代码库，但实际上在大的软件项目中，程序员只理解自己负责的一小部分代码是常态。

想象一下，新人去接手一个历史复杂项目，那么他们短时间只可能理解一部分代码，但这并不妨碍他们去维护项目。

那么以前怎么保证不理解完整代码不会改出问题呢？还得要靠自动化测试来兜底。

一个好的项目，需要配合好充分的自动化测试覆盖，这样就算新手去修改代码，也不至于把正常运行的系统搞崩溃，毕竟改出问题了自动化测试是无法通过的。

并且为了防止新人乱改，还会有 Code Review 配合，这本身也是很好的知识传承手段。

现在让 Agent 干活也是如此，让 Agent 在一个会话上下文中理解整个项目是不现实的，它永远只能部分理解项目，但这并不妨碍 Agent 去修改运行程序。

要保证 Agent 干活的质量，同样也要通过验证手段兜底，自动化测试是必须的，但也无法过度依赖，因为有些测试可能本身就是有问题的；

Code Review 现在也很难保证了，毕竟代码量太大了，人根本看不过来，只能是让 AI Review 大部分代码，人只 Review 最重要的部分。

另外一个有效手段就是让 Agent 自己提供证据，比如我最近最常用的手段就是让 Agent 截图，在开发新功能的时候让它提供新功能截图，修改 bug 的时候提供改之前和改之后的截图对比。

让 Agent 截图，最近还挖掘出来一个用法：就是让 Agent 自己去模拟 API 响应数据，动态生成各种不同场景的截图，都不需要服务端配合，虽然我还没搞明白它是怎么去模拟的。

quoted_tweet.author: Sean Goedecke
quoted_tweet.text: In many software engineering environments, there’s nothing wrong with being in a state of partial understanding. In fact, in large systems a partial understanding is the best you can do.

text:
as some of u may have suspected, i have recently joined @METR_Evals  :)

this is one of the first things i worked on there, along w the rest of the capabilities team, very excited it's finally out. understanding what the hell is going on with models and especially where their remaining gaps are is incredibly critical for informing our decision making as a species.

there's a shitload of stuff in here, really excited for people to wade into the appendices, and i've even made sure to make all the backing data behind charts easy to download so ppl don't have to do pixel peeping to claude up their own charts. 

some random (personal) takeaways:
- it would be really sick if time horizons continued to work as an easily interpretable measure of capability... but unfortunately i think that's just no longer true. there's just too much variance in the spikes.
- as much as i'd love for IRT methods to result in *intuitive* understanding they're just kinda structurally very uninterpretable, but remain basically our best way to get ~reasonably robust aggregate info
- swarms are complicated! model behavior in swarms is super sensitive to all kinds of factors, inter-run variance is high, "swarm cultures" can form and significantly affect performance. for some things, clear strong uplift! for others, swarms are a downlift. love it when u get results that are basically "haha good luck making a trend outta this"
- getting humans to outperform models is really rough now. really extremely rough. even with some model assistance, for basically everything verifiable we're pretty much at the point where only ~world class experts still beat models, and it's hard af to get world class experts to spend two straight months working on a METR task
- it's pretty crazy watching models advance past what you thought was potentially possible on a task, and then go further, and then further, until you're just no longer sure where the upper limit actually is

somewhat more personally, on the Tenobrus account. historically i feel like i've actually done a lot of good for safety by being a "brawler", wading into fights, saying things i thought were true regardless of consequences, saying shit that i just kinda thought was funny at the time... for a long long time, my account has reflected on no one but me.

but i don't think i can really remain in that place while at METR. it would be disingenuous to remain anon and speak without disclosing my affiliations while working for the transparency organization. it's 2026, it's crunch time, it's time to step up and try to provide the kind of independent and carefully truthful institutions the world needs rn. so my style here is gonna change. that's okay, it's already been changing for a long time! and METR is worth it, i think it's one of the single most impactful places in the world to be right now, and i'm not going to fuck up that responsibility.

let's keep figuring this shit out :)
